Kesinlikle old-school korku sevenlerin ilgisini çekebilecek bir oyun.

 Bu oyunu ilk defa çok eskiden başka bir platformdan oynarken bana inanılmaz korkutucu gelmişti. Sanırım enemy movement ve spawn noktaları ile safe zoneları öğrenince oyun, beni eskisi kadar korkutamadı. 2.5D olmasına rağmen bol bol jumpscare elementleri var. Genelde jumpscare'ları hiç sevmesem de bu oyun serisi bunu oldukça iyi kullanyor, çünkü oyunun yapısı gereği zaten yukarıdan görüşünüz her şeyi olduğu gibi görebilmenize olanak sağlıyorken enemy'nin önünüze teleport olabilmesi, karanlık bölgelerin görüşünüzü sınırlaması, el fenerinin sınırlı kullanım ömrünün olması, oyundaki genel sessizliğin bir anda bozulabilmesi gibi etkenler oyunu bence FNAF benzeri bir korku oyunu yapabilmiş. Her ne kadar FNAF tarzı jumpscare'ları sevmesem de bu oyun bunu çok cheesy yapmamış.

 FNAF ve Friday The 13th temalarını çok yoğun hissedebilirsiniz: Jumpscare atan maskot bir ayıcık gençlerin olduğu kamp alanında herkesi şeytani bir güçle öldürüyor. Yine de aradaki boşlukları doldururken özgün kalıp bundan iyi bir hikaye çıkartmayı başarıyor. Final kısmı hariç çok zor değildi, lakin oyunu ilk oynarken çok fazla save aldığımı ve tam hatırlayamasam da kendimi softlock yaptığımı, kaydımı geri yüklemek zorunda kaldığımı hatırlıyorum.

 Ünideyken bu oyunu sınıfımdaki nerdeyse hiç oyun oynamayan çocuğa önermiş olduğuma da hala inanamıyorum. Herhalde oyunu o an cidden çok sevmiştim. Tabii çocukla daha sonra muhattabım da olmayınca oyunu oynayıp oynamadığını bile öğrenemedim. Old-school ve retro korku eramdı, yaptık bir hata diyelim.

I absolutely LOVED this game! Despite the playtime registered it took me 6h:45m to complete, but this was spent offline while travelling.

I had just finished Terror at Oakheart and was looking for something similar and this more than fit the bill!

Where to start? At the beginning I guess. I really liked the premise and concept, it grabbed me from the off and never really let go. The story was strong throughout.

I LOVED the Easter-egg type references to the movies that inspired it, and it is a testament to the wonderful pixel artists that I was able to recognise the tiny pixelated movie posters - great job!

I did find the antagonist a bit annoying at times - the way he could spawn right next to you at times, but I soon learned that if you kept stocked up on food this was bearable (no pun intended :). 

As well as great graphics the sound design was BRILLIANT - I particularly loved the strangulated sounds some victims made. The game was full of humour, and I found one hilariously brilliant easter-egg just by chance [spoiler] (think of the age old struggle between men and women in the bathroom). [/spoiler]  

I also found a bit of help along the way. [spoiler] The 'heating engineer' had extremely deep pockets (at least during my playthrough). [/spoiler]

The puzzles were not too taxing - apart from one end game one, which required a bit of trial and error - but they were all enjoyable.

Finally, I have to admit I almost shed a tear at the end!

To sum things up, when I love a game I always look to see what other games the devs have released and I was over the moon to see they had made a prequel (Sunshine Manor) so this was an instant purchase and I cannot wait to play this, and will keep an eye out for future releases from this team.

Though this top-down adventure looks and plays like an RPG Maker game, the finer touches set it off.  The creepy lighting is good at generating jumpy moments despite the overall parodic nature of things.  Your map of slasher-haunted Camp Sunshine is easy to use, and quest locations are marked so you don't ever need to whip out the ol' notebook.  The horror movie references are sincere and don't feel forced ([i]most[/i] of the time).  

While the humor is of the jejune, gross-out variety that ever appeals to eternal children like me, it's occasionally undercut by unpolished or just plain [i]flat[/i] writing -- the team could certainly have used an extra editor or two.  A few rough patches, however, don't detract much from the experience.  The story is actually pretty damned decent for the slasher genre, and there's always some new place to go, some new thing to see -- and that, friends, is one of the true strengths of short, well-made games like this:  you'll never get bored, and the padding is never such that the fundamental [i]feel[/i] of the adventure has time to slip through your fingers.  Mini-adventures for the win!  We need more of 'em!

[h1] Genre [/h1] Ein Survival Horror Adventure

[h1] Story [/h1] Wir spielen einen Jungen Namens "Jez" und werden von unserer Mutter ins "Camp Sunshine" gebracht um dort 1 Woche Spaß zu haben. Kaum ist unsere Mutter wieder gegangen, verwandelt sich dieser Camp Ausflug in einen Kampf ums Überleben, denn etwas Böses ist hier am Werk

[h1] Gameplay [/h1] Hauptziel des Spiels ist es Tagebucheinträge zu finden um mehr über die Story und den Mörder herauszufinden. In jedem Tagebucheintrag wird außerdem immer ein bestimmter Gegenstand genannt, die wir finden müssen. Man kann die Gegenstände natürlich auch schon eingesammelt haben, bevor man das bestimmte Tagebucheintrag gelesen hat. Wir laufen durch das doch recht Große Camp und durchsuchen verschiedene Gebäude nach Gegenständen und treffen ab und an auch mal auf Überlebende, für die wir dann eine kleine Aufgabe erledigen müssen. Natürlich können wir dies alles nicht in ruhe und frieden erledigen, denn ein Killer in einem Bären Kostüm und mit einem Messer bewaffnet ist auf ständiger Jagd nach uns. Man kann jeweils einmal vom Killer getroffen werden ohne zu sterben, wenn dies passiert, verschwindet der Killer für eine gewisse Zeit. Natürlich können wir uns mit "Food" heilen um immer wieder einen Angriff auszuhalten. man kann dem Killer aber auch recht einfach ausweichen. Man hat eine Taschenlampe die natürlich Batterien benötigt aber doch sehr nützlich ist. Man kann auch sprinten aber auch nicht lange, Stamina lässt sich durch "Energiedrinks" wieder aufladen oder wenn man eine Kurze Zeit lang wartet. Es gibt zudem auch ein paar recht Nette Kleine Rätsel zu lösen und einige Nette Easter Eggs für Horror Film Fans. Die Atmosphäre, die Musik und die Soundeffekte sind wirklich Top

I'd describe Camp Sunshine as a modern horror game made in a JRPG engine. You search for the 8 pages of a diary to learn about and to defeat a masked serial killer. Along the way you encounter NPCs who need you to fetch stuff, corpses and drawers to loot for items, and evade the Killer by running and hiding in bushes.

Obviously, the gameplay isn't deep but the developers put a ton of work into the theme. The atmosphere is top notch and the developers played to their strengths. While the story is stereotypical and shallow, they literally hang their green and red sweaters of inspiration on the walls. It's full of references without compromising the tension they've created.  

At the end of the day, this feels like a passion project. Just like the movies it's tries to emulate, it has more heart than it does budget but this helps it shine. The devs didn't set out to win GOTY, but to create a fun horror experience and they succeeded.

It's not deep, it's not long lasting, but it's well-made. If you love horror games and movies this is well-worth a sale purchase.

Muni d'un esprit fermé, on peut penser que les jeux d'horreur se limitent aux titres en 3D 
(Resident Evil, Dead Space, Siren...), car il est vrai que ces types de jeux on beaucoup servis à définir le genre actuel.
Au final on se rend compte via "Camp Sunshine" que le genre est plus riche que ça. 
Si la mise en scène n'est pas aussi terrifiante que dans d'autres jeux (cela dépends des goûts certes), l'ambiance horrifique est bien respecté et provoque de bon moments de stress par moment. En particulier quand l'ours tueur apparaît dans la peine ombre. 
Toutefois j'aurais apprécié que des situations imprévues soient plus présentes (ours caché derrière du mobilier...) car la dangerosité du tueur ne se fait pas assez ressentir. L'environnement et l'ambiance sont plus là pour ça.
Optez pour le mode difficile de base si vous recherchez ce challenge, il devrais être meilleur que le mien.


Globalement "Camp Sunshine" est un jeu d'aventure horrifique où vous incarnez un jeune campeur au sein d'un univers macabre.
Axé d'un point de vue Gameplay sur l'exploration et la recherche d'indices, votre but sera de comprendre les raisons de cette tuerie et de vaincre l'ours tueur afin de vous échapper de cet enfer. Le tout devrais vous occuper environ 4 heures. 
Si l'histoire dramatique est plutôt intéressante, sachez que le jeu ne soit dispo qu'en anglais. De même, les touches du clavier ne sont pas remappables. Ainsi si vous jouer via le clavier, privilégiez les touches directionnelles pour vous déplacez. Moins chiant que le "WASD" anglais. Enfin, si vous avez perdus patience dans la recherche d'indice (car vous avez l'obligation de trouver tous les artefacts pour accéder à la fin), sachez qu'un glossaire est dispo sur steam pour vous aiguiller. Merci la communauté.

Bref, en soi "Camp Sunshine" est un bon petit jeu d'horreur en 2D. Dommage qu'une exploration un peu trop insistante et une difficulté moindre viennent entacher cela.

Gameplay is slender-esque and has typical aspects of RPGMaker horror games. Explore, find items, do things...
With the decently sized map, it gives variety with the different buildings, and incentive to go into all of them (You pretty much have to explore everything anyway) whether you wanna see more spooks, or need more resources. Overall, a lot of exploring, foraging, and running away. Since there are so many things to collect, I sometimes forgot what I had to do, but fortunately for me I had a friend on call who was playing the game as well, and we helped each other for the collecting.
[b] GAMEPLAY: .90/1 [/b]

For the story, the notes you collect on you journey keep you a bit compelled, but it is nothing too special, however it works for this type of game. There are story aspects of the game that never really get clarified, and no closure about the few other characters that might have survived in the end. Especially around the end, the story gets.....weird. 
[b] STORY: .70/1 [/b]

Camp Sunshine doesn't take itself seriously sometimes, which can be quite amusing. The main character Jez, seems like one of the few normal people out here, as you meet many other weirdos who somehow survived. This isn't the kind of game where you would have major character development or anything. The Camp as I said before, is fun to explore and does have a tense atmosphere in the beginning. But like many other horror games with monsters that hunt you, once you get good it's not that scary anymore. You remember the paths that have sticks, and ones that don't, and you have mastered the art of escaping Sunshine Bear. (Who's voice in amazing btw)
[b] CHARACTERS/WORLD: .80/1 [/b]

These retro graphics for an RPG, are polished and nice, even though you will most likely be in darkness for the majority of the game, it's not difficult to travel around places, which is a huge plus for me.The music that does play is reminiscent of classic horror movie music and fits the game very well. I also only encountered 1 bug while playing through the game. At one point, Jez would be facing forward every where he moved (for example if you moved down he would be moonwalking) it didn't affect the game really at all, and it fixed itself once I saved, it just made it slightly harder to interact with objects that way. There was also a scene at the end that lagged really badly on my computer for some reason. I could see myself helping a friend to play this game, but there is not that much replay value to it, which is expected. 
[b] GRAPHICS: 1/1 [/b]
[b] MUSIC: 1/1 [/b]
[b] OPTIMIZATION/BUGS: .80/1 [/b]
[b] REPLAY VALUE: .60/1 [/b]

This game was quite memorable since I sorta played it with a friend. Especially hearing Sunshine Bear's voice for the first few times was terrifying! In conclusion, this game did not have much down time and progressed smoothly, leading to a fun experience that didn't get very boring. For the 2-4 hours of fun you could get out of this, it's worth the full price of $3, definitely pick up on sale if you like these sort of games.

The gameplay is simple: Walk around, interact with things, find items, and avoid enemies. The game is semi open-world in that you can tackle the majority of the item-collecting around the camp in whatever route you choose, however the key story moments play out in the same places.

Don't let the fact that this game was made with RPG Maker put you off, it's actually a very enjoyable experience.

Camp Sunshine thrusts you into the shoes of Jez, a boy being sent to summer camp while his parents figure out stuff between the two of them. Jez arrives, meets a few people, and then settles in for the night. Upon waking he discovers that there is something very wrong going down at Camp Sunshine -- bloody bodies are everywhere, and that's just the beginning of this nightmare. Your job is to guide him through Camp Sunshine finding the various clues, pages, etc. that open up more of the story as you progress. The story is engaging enough to keep you pushing through the game and the difficulty isn't so bad that you can't handle things. 

My advice for new players would be that if you're looking for JUST a story experience then play this on Easy. You will literally find so much supplies throughout the game that getting hit or using up batteries isn't an issue. I played on Easy so I can't say how much harder the other difficulties are but if you are looking for something that isn't a 100% cakewalk seek out Normal/Hard mode. There are some minor frame stutters in the game at times as well but they aren't too terrible to deal with. Dodging/running away from the enemy is also not terribly hard.

A final note about this game: It's hidden gems like these that make you think twice before overlooking RPG maker games for the sole reason they were "made in RPG maker", so I want to say thank you to the creators for creating this little gem.
